source.title: From Oragnized Shelves to Layered Catalogs: Architectural Explorations for Sparse Autoencoders -- Crosscoders & Ladder SAEs Towards Hierarchical Data Structure

record.tranche_reason: Reports sparse latent coding and reconstruction results for crosscoders on GPT-2, an LLM setting relevant to V4, but does not reproduce the toy-model experiments.
record.gate_note: The reported crosscoder sparsity and reconstruction results bear indirectly on sparse dictionary representations in an LLM. The post does not measure features spread across neurons, feature importance, or superposition geometry. Ladder SAE experiments are pending. The neighborhood-recovery results measure preservation of an externally supplied sentence graph, not the behavior named by any claim version.
record.test_reason: The post trains crosscoder variants (Vanilla L1, isotropic Gaussian, sentence-graph penalty) on GPT-2 and compares their reconstruction, sparsity and neighbourhood-recovery metrics. These are performance numbers for the authors' own method against alternatives. No result bears on whether a version of superposition holds. It never checks that latents are interpretable or recovered model features, never measures features spread across neurons, and runs no toy-model or capacity tests. Ladder SAE results are pending. It uses the superposition/SAE framing as motivation only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that a structured graph penalty can replace L1 to give sparse, high-fidelity crosscoder latents. They say the isotropic Gaussian prior lacks the right inductive bias, and that the graph regulariser better preserves local semantic neighbourhoods (top-k precision). They attribute Vanilla's small NDCG edge to asymmetric kNN graphs. Ladder SAE results are pending.
record.recipe_differences: The post trains GPT-2 crosscoders with sentence-graph or isotropic priors and outlines Ladder SAEs; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported sparsity and fidelity differ across Vanilla, Gaussian-iso, and Graph configurations. Neighborhood-recovery comparisons also vary by metric cutoff.

fits_no_version.finding: On GPT-2 (TinyStories), a sentence-graph Laplacian penalty without L1 gave 84.7% dead latents and R² 0.935. This compares with 92.8% dead and R² 0.940 for L1. An isotropic Gaussian KL prior gave R² 0.687 and 13.2% dead.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A structured (graph-Laplacian) penalty can substitute for L1 in inducing sparse, high-fidelity crosscoder latents, while isotropic priors cannot.

fits_no_version.finding: Compared with Vanilla, the graph crosscoder has slightly higher Precision@64 (0.0134 vs 0.0129), parity at @128 and lower at @256. NDCG is marginally lower at all cutoffs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Graph-regularized crosscoders preserve external sentence-graph neighbourhoods slightly better at top-k, with cutoff-dependent and very small differences.

record.problems: The results are presented in flattened tables without uncertainty estimates. The reported crosscoder latents are not validated as recovered model features; the graph is externally constructed, the study uses GPT-2 only, and Ladder SAE experiments are pending.
record.rows_left_out: The reconstruction-error columns in Table 2 were not extracted because the flattened values could not be assigned confidently to the stated MSE columns.

untested.parts: No toy networks, feature/dimension sweep, sparsity transition, or geometry analysis.
No test of capacity competition or feature importance.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.

No measure of features distributed across neurons. Crosscoder latents are not validated as model features (no interpretability or causal checks); only reconstruction and sparsity of the tool are reported.
No completeness, stability or canonicality test of dictionary features.
No test of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features. Ladder SAE hierarchy experiments are pending.

record.verdict_notes: This is an architecture/method post (LessWrong, SPAR project), not a test of superposition. The reader's V4 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels were removed. They rested on the study's own method compared with alternatives, which is excluded under T4. Neighbourhood differences are tiny and have no uncertainty reported. The Table 2 MSE columns are flattened ambiguously but bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-over-capacity sweep, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular superposition geometry are tested.
No test of capacity pressure, dedicated dimensions for important features, or competition between features.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.

The evidence is crosscoder latent sparsity and activation reconstruction on GPT-2; it does not test features distributed across neurons or validate that the learned latents are recovered model features.
No completeness, stability, or canonicality test of SAE features.
No test of whether model features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Vanilla and Graph crosscoders on GPT-2
reader_labels.reason: Both configurations report high reconstruction R² alongside sparse latents (rows r1–r3 and r7–r9), providing indirect evidence that sparse learned codes can represent GPT-2 activations.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: This configuration has much lower reported dead-latent proportion and R² than Vanilla, so the sparse-code result depends on the training configuration (rows r4–r6).
